messages.subject: Hierarchical subject metadataSpeciesTag not found
parts:
Hello camtrapR users and Juergen,

I'm getting to grips with camtrapR for a very large data set and am testing out the metadatatag usage for each species captured on CT. At present I'm testing it out on an image, which has been renamed, copied to a new folder and tagged in DigiKam according to the hierarchical structure of 'Species' > 'Banteng'. Write to sidecard is not selected. When I check the properties of the images in DigiKam I can clearly see the correct tags, and also in R when I run head(rec.db.Banteng) I can see the tags are present in the HierarchicalSubject (i.e. 'Species|Banteng'). When I try and extract the RecordTable for 'Species', all works fine. When I add the addition of metadataSpeciesTag ="Banteng" and extract the RecordTable I get the following error:

DFRCT001 : 1 images
Warning: DFRCT001:   metadataSpeciesTag 'Banteng' not found in image metadata tag 'HierarchicalSubject'.
Error: something went wrong. I looked through all those 1 folders and now your table is empty. Did you exclude too many species? Or were date/time information not readable?

I've tried retagging with a new structure (according to the Vignette: Extracting Data from Camera Trapping Images), reinstalling and using different images but still with the same error. My folder structure is: D drive > RenamedImages > Station > CameraA > Species > Banteng. I'm sure it's something simple but I've not been able to get pass this issue and now need a fresh pair of eyes on it. I've already looked through the forum to avoid reposting the same problem but have been unable to solve it from those posts. I've attached the CT image I've been using and the script is below. If someone is able to take a look then I really appreciate it.


PG_wd_StationDir <- file.path("D:/RenamedImages")

Banteng_files <- list.files(PG_wd_StationDir, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)

rec.db.Banteng <- recordTable(inDir  = PG_wd_StationDir,
IDfrom = "metadata",
cameraID = "filename",
camerasIndependent = FALSE,
minDeltaTime = 0,
deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastRecord",
timeZone ="Asia/Kuala_Lumpur",
writecsv = TRUE,
outDir = "D:/RenamedImages",
metadataSpeciesTag ="Banteng",
metadataHierarchyDelimitor = "|",
removeDuplicateRecords = TRUE)

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Hierarchical subject metadataSpeciesTag not found
parts:
Hi Penny, 
you set up the tag structure in digiKam correctly (hierarchical tag structure of 'Species' > 'Banteng').

The problem is in the argument metadataSpeciesTag = "Banteng". Instead of bantang (the species name) you need to set it to:

metadataSpeciesTag ="Species"

The argument metadataSpeciesTag specifies the name of the tag group that contains the species tags, not the species tag you are interested in. Hence it must be "Species", not "Banteng". 

If you are only interested in records of banteng, I recommend you simply subset the record table after running the recordTable function.

Best regards,
Jürgen
